title: auth: clarify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need to standardize auth/header semantics across the Redwood API and the OpenAI compatibility layer to support project vs org keys, scoped 'session' tokens, CORS preflight behavior for browser clients, and optional request signing using a nonce header. This PR consolidates behaviors, documents expectations, and adds guards to avoid accidental token exposure or ambiguous behavior when multiple auth headers are present.

Summary of changes: 1) Header precedence rules: added canonical parsing order (Redwood-Project, Authorization Bearer, X-Redwood-Scope, x-redwood-nonce). When both project and org keys are presented we now prefer explicit project-scoped headers and surface a debug log when fallback occurs. 2) Scoped/session tokens: introduce semantics for "Scoped-Token" (x-redwood-scoped-token) for short-lived, scope-limited tokens used by third-party embed flows; validation is enforced in the token middleware and documented in the OpenAPI compat layer. 3) Nonce/request signing: add optional X-Redwood-Nonce header and an HMAC verification hook (configurable per-tenant) to support signed requests for webhooks and client-side signing flows; the header is ignored unless signing is enabled for the tenant. 4) CORS: update CORS preflight to expose supported headers and confirm that Bearer tokens are not allowed in browsers unless using the dedicated/embed flow with scoped tokens; preflight rejects requests with sensitive headers unless the tenant opted into browser clients. 5) OpenAI compatibility: align our Authorization header parsing to accept both "Bearer <token>" and the legacy "OpenAI-Key: <token>" used in some customers' proxies, mapping legacy headers to the canonical Authorization internally. 6) SDK and examples: TypeScript + Python SDKs updated with helpers for scoped tokens and nonce signing examples. 7) Docs: extensive docs updates and a migration note for customers who rely on mixed header behavior.

Commits summary: "Initial middleware + docs"; "Add nonce HMAC hook and tests"; "CORS preflight header exposure and opt-in flag"; "SDK helpers and examples"; "tests: add token parsing unit/integration tests"; "fix: lint and type issues after review".

Files changed (high level): src/api/auth/middleware.go; src/api/auth/header_parsing.go; src/api/auth/nonce_verifier.go; src/api/cors/cors.go; internal/compat/openai/header_adapter.go; sdk/typescript/src/auth.ts; sdk/python/redwood/auth.py; docs/auth/header-semantics.md; tests/integration/auth_headers_test.go; tests/unit/nonce_test.go; README-MIGRATION.md.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for header precedence, scoped-token validation, nonce signing verification, and CORS preflight behavior. Integration tests simulate browser + embedded client flows. CI initially failed on lint/typecheck due to naming differences in the SDK, fixed in follow-up commit. Final CI: all checks passed (unit/integration/lint/contract tests).

Rollout plan: Feature is behind a tenant feature flag (auth-header-v2). Default tenants continue with prior behavior. We will enable gradually for early adopters after a short canary run; migration docs include a checklist for customers using proxies that inject legacy headers.

Notes: - This PR intentionally does not flip default behavior cluster-wide; operators must enable auth-header-v2 and request-signing per-tenant. - There is a documented deprecation timeline for legacy OpenAI-Key header in the docs.

release_notes: Clarify auth header semantics: new precedence rules, scoped session tokens, optional nonce-based request signing, stricter CORS for browser flows, and OpenAI header mapping. Backwards compatible by default behind a tenant feature-flag. SDK helpers and examples included.
security_impact: Medium - introduces optional signing and new header semantics. Default behaviour is unchanged until tenant opt-in. Reviewers requested and received additional telemetry and key rotation support.
migration_steps: 1) Read docs/auth/header-semantics.md and README-MIGRATION.md. 2) If you accept browser-embed flows, opt-in on tenant via admin UI or API flag. 3) Rotate any proxy that emits OpenAI-Key to emit Authorization: Bearer or enable compat mapping. 4) If using request signing, provision signing key via admin API and enable per-tenant. 5) Run tests against staging (integration/auth_headers_test.go) before enabling in prod.
follow_up: ENG-3498: audit all public examples to ensure they don't recommend using long-lived org keys in browsers; ENG-3521: rollout plan telemetry to track how many tenants enable auth-header-v2 in first 30 days.
